Statement of Work paragraph 2.1 requires documented evidence of past performance migrating legacy Microsoft Access systems to Microsoft 365 and the Power Platform. Two questions on this paragraph: a. Is 2.1 a pass or fail responsibility requirement, or is it evaluated as part of the past performance factor described in the evaluation criteria? b. Where an offeror's relevant past performance was performed under commercial contracts rather than federal prime contracts, will the Government accept that commercial past performance? Will the Government also accept the relevant past performance of proposed key personnel or of a proposed subcontractor? Answer: Paragraph 2.1 is evaluated as part of the Government’s technical assessment of the offeror’s relevant past performance and technical competency, rather than as a separate pass/fail responsibility determination. The Government will accept relevant commercial past performance, not just federal prime contract experience, provided the quoted experience demonstrates comparable scope, complexity, and relevance to the requirement. Section G requires certification documentation for Microsoft 365 and SharePoint Online. May the offeror satisfy this requirement with certifications held by named key personnel who will perform the work, or must the certifications be held at the offeror entity level? The MHS is unique in that it functions as both a direct healthcare provider and a multi-billion-dollar health insurance payer through the TRICARE program. It is a globally integrated system serving over 9.6 million beneficiaries, including active-duty service members, retirees, and their families. The MHS is unique in that it functions as both a direct healthcare provider and a multi-billion-dollar health insurance payer through the TRICARE program. Its ultimate success

e medical capabilities, austere mission environments, field hospitals and Forward Operating Bases. DoW’s close relationship with the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is paramount. Equally critical is the ability to support the continuum of care across operational and enterprise healthcare environments, ensuring that health information generated during military operations can be captured, exchanged, and made available to support continued care within the enterprise health record.
